newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady, two cargoes traded at $99/T.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Steady, two cargoes traded at $99/T.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil bids outnumbered offers on Monday but prices remained stuck in a range, traders said.

Late in the Asian trading day, two 180-cst cargoes were traded at $99.00 per tonne fob Singapore, lifting July 22-26 and another lifting August 2-6 at the same price. The two cargoes were sold by a European major and another by US major to the same local trader who has been an active buyers in the past two weeks.
The local trader has to date purchased 160,000 tonnes of fuel oil for July and August loading.

The trader said the market is fundamentally strong. While some majors said the trader is buying to fulfil its term commitments, the trader said he is selling some of its supplies in the bunker market.
Taiwan has issued a tender to sell 30,000 tonnes of fuel oil for August 1-5 loading. The tender closes July 15 and is valid for two days.
Swaps were also steady with July and August last quoted at $98.50/$99.25, little changed from levels on Friday.
Sentiment in the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) remained strong. Reduced allocations from Indonesia and a heatwave in Japan is expected to boost levels up.
Indonesia has allocated a total of just 2.3 million barrels in July. Spot Indonesian cargoes were assessed at $1.10 to $1.50 per barrel over the Pertamina formula, fob.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
